title: Create safety and hold tests
description:
Create tests/SafetyHoldTests.cpp using the built-in juce::UnitTest framework and register it in CMakeLists.txt on the existing console test-runner target. This is a serialized CMakeLists.txt write: it runs after f.7 and before f.9.

Before editing, inspect:
- Source/DSP/SafetyProcessor.h (limiter enable, ceiling application, intervention flag, buffer-clear request)
- Source/DSP/DelayVoice.h (Hold engage/release surface)
- tests/RoutingBypassTests.cpp (the juce::UnitTest idiom established by f.7)
- CMakeLists.txt (the console test-runner target and its target_sources list)

Required test coverage — stimuli: impulses, full-scale tones, silence, denormal-range values (magnitudes near 1e-30), NaN, infinity, maximum feedback, and DC. For every stimulus assert: no NaN or infinity in the output, no runaway amplitude growth over a bounded run, the test completes within a bounded sample count (no hang), and the atomic safety-intervention flag is published when an invalid state was injected.

Additional required assertions:
- With the optional RMS limiter disabled, the mandatory layer is still active: the 0.985 feedback ceiling still applies, NaN and infinity are still rejected, and the DC blocker still removes a constant offset.
- With the limiter enabled, sustained input above the 0.90 linear threshold produces a feedback gain reduction consistent with reduction = min(1, 0.90/(energy+epsilon)) and g_safe = min(0.985, g_requested*reduction).
- Hold kills new delay input: feed a burst, engage Hold, feed further input, and assert the held tail contains no contribution from the post-engage input.
- Hold bypasses tone processing so the held tail stays spectrally stable: compare a coarse spectral measure (for example high-band to low-band energy ratio via band-limited RMS) at the start and after several seconds of held repeats and assert it stays within a stated tolerance, demonstrating no progressive darkening.
- Hold gain caps at 0.985 and Hold release is click-free against an explicit sample-delta threshold across the 30 ms crossfade.

NaN and infinity injection occurs only inside this test file; production code must not be modified to enable it.

Use only juce::UnitTest. Catch2, GoogleTest, and every other third-party framework are forbidden, and no new dependency may be introduced. Tests must be deterministic: fixed sample rates, fixed block sizes, fixed generated signals, no wall-clock dependence.

In CMakeLists.txt, add only tests/SafetyHoldTests.cpp to the existing test-runner target sources.

tests/SafetyHoldTests.cpp asserts Hold admits no post-engage delay input and that Hold gain does not exceed 0.985
tests/SafetyHoldTests.cpp asserts a band-energy ratio of the held tail stays within a stated tolerance over several seconds of repeats, demonstrating no progressive darkening
